additions.reason: Eretz Yisrael is the dominant concept of this Torah — it is the holy reality that the tzaddik's burial place shares in nature, and it is also described as a great tikkun for the blemish of the Brit. It appears in both the bechina relationship (burial place IS Eretz Yisrael in holiness) and in the eitza relationship (Eretz Yisrael → repairs the brit). It is the central node of Package 1.
additions.source_quote: הַצַּדִּיקִים אֲמִתִּיִּים יוֹרְשִׁים אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁזּוֹכִין שֶׁמְּקוֹם גְּנִיזָתָם הוּא קָדוֹשׁ בִּקְדֻשַּׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל מַמָּשׁ

additions.reason: The burial/concealment place of the true tzaddik is explicitly stated to share the essential holiness of Eretz Yisrael itself. 'מְקוֹם גְּנִיזָתָם הוּא קָדוֹשׁ בִּקְדֻשַּׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל מַמָּשׁ' — the tzaddik's burial place IS holy with the holiness of Eretz Yisrael. This is a direct bechina: burial place ↔ Eretz Yisrael in essential nature.
additions.source_quote: מְקוֹם גְּנִיזָתָם הוּא קָדוֹשׁ בִּקְדֻשַּׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל מַמָּשׁ

additions.reason: The holiness of Eretz Yisrael is the quality that the tzaddik's burial place acquires. It is the essential nature shared between ארץ ישראל and מקום גניזה. Naming it separately reflects that the Rebbe emphasizes the specific qualitative holiness ('ממש' — literally/actually), not merely a metaphorical comparison.
additions.source_quote: מְקוֹם גְּנִיזָתָם הוּא קָדוֹשׁ בִּקְדֻשַּׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל מַמָּשׁ

additions.reason: True tzaddikim are the agents of the Eretz Yisrael holiness-transfer. The Rebbe's teaching is precisely about who 'inherits' Eretz Yisrael in this sense — only the 'true tzaddikim' (as opposed to those who merely call themselves tzaddikim). They are not metaphorically equated with Eretz Yisrael, but they are the persons through whom the bechina of the burial place = Eretz Yisrael is actualized. They belong in Package 1 as a key component of the same domain.

notes_on_unpackaged_concepts.reason: The blemish of the Brit appears in the Torah's final sentence as the target of an eitza relationship: ארץ ישראל IS a great tikkun FOR the blemish of the Brit. This is a directional, cause-and-effect statement — Eretz Yisrael repairs/rectifies the brit-blemish. There is no bechina language connecting פגם הברית to any other concept in this Torah, and it has no bechina partners. It stands alone as the negative reality that Eretz Yisrael (Package 1) repairs via an eitza. It is NOT included in Package 1, as it represents the opposing/negative domain, and is not stated to share the nature of Eretz Yisrael. It could form its own 1-node 'package' (evil polarity), but since there are no bechina connections to anchor it, it is documented here as an unpackaged eitza-node.

The 'great tikkun' is a descriptor of what Eretz Yisrael accomplishes for פגם הברית. It is not an independent concept with bechina connections; it characterizes the eitza relationship between ארץ ישראל and פגם הברית. No separate package.

analysis_notes.torah_argument_flow: Package 1 (Eretz Yisrael / burial place of the tzaddik) is the positive holy domain. The tzaddik's grave IS Eretz Yisrael (bechina). Eretz Yisrael then serves as a great rectification for the blemish of the Brit (eitza, outgoing from Package 1 to the negative concept of פגם הברית). The Torah is extremely brief with one bechina and one eitza statement.
